submission.justification: While Absorber-F2 at 3mm provides the best energy resolution (3.201%), the critical constraint requiring hands-on maintenance during shutdowns makes it unsuitable. Dense high-Z alloys (F2 and F3) in the forward region of a collider detector become highly activated from beam interactions, producing long-lived radioactive isotopes that prevent hands-on access. Absorber-F1, described as a "standard structural absorber," is the only material that can satisfy the hands-on maintenance requirement. Among all plate thicknesses tested for F1, 5mm provides the best energy resolution at 5.089%. This represents an acceptable compromise between achieving good energy resolution and meeting the essential operational constraint for maintenance accessibility.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 at 5mm achieves 5.089% resolution, which is the best achievable while satisfying the hands-on maintenance constraint. This is the optimal result among viable options (tested 2-10mm range for F1).

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md as one of the three candidate materials.

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns
requirements.evidence: Absorber-F1 is described as a 'standard structural absorber' which indicates lower activation properties suitable for hands-on maintenance, unlike the dense high-Z alloys (F2, F3) which would become highly activated in the forward region.
Recommended thickness of 5mm is within the specified range of 2-10mm.
